in_game_claim: Bandage at night against fever and headache; infusion against chills and dizziness
real_world_finding: EMA accepts only traditional use for temporary loss of appetite and mild stomach/gut complaints (bitter taste stimulates the gut); fever and headache are not among the accepted uses
rule_direction: Appetite/digestion side effect is defensible; fever and headache claims are not

in_game_claim: Greatly increases strength and dispels fatigue but lowers speech
real_world_finding: No real-world basis found; this is a game mechanic
rule_direction: Keep the in-game buff; do not justify it with pharmacology

in_game_claim: (not in game text) toxicity of the herb
real_world_finding: Thujone is neurotoxic; convulsions at high doses; EMA limits intake to a few mg/day for at most 2 weeks
rule_direction: Possible class B rule: large or repeated doses carry a risk (direction only)

in_game_claim: Very poisonous; shakes and chills; convulsions and strange visions; a small amount can kill
real_world_finding: Tropane alkaloids (atropine, hyoscyamine, scopolamine) cause an anticholinergic syndrome: dry skin, dilated pupils, fast heart, agitation, hallucinations, seizures; onset about 1-4 h
rule_direction: Justifies health loss and hallucination-style debuffs; magnitude is a balance choice

in_game_claim: Dispels sickness; quiets fever and period pains; infusion soothes the stomach
real_world_finding: EMA accepts minor gastro-intestinal complaints and spasms, skin and wound use, mouth and throat inflammation; fever and period pain are not accepted uses
rule_direction: Mild digestive benefit is defensible

in_game_claim: Combined with the wrong herb it induces too deep a sleep
real_world_finding: NCCIH: possible interaction with sedatives and some liver-metabolised drugs; allergy in ragweed-allergic people
rule_direction: Sedative stacking with poppy/valerian is plausible

in_game_claim: Best remedy for broken bones; swelling and bruising; internal bone pain
real_world_finding: EMA traditional use is EXTERNAL only (minor sprains and bruises, adults, up to about 10 days); 'adjuvant after fractures' appears only in historical registrations
rule_direction: A topical/bandage item would fit; a drinkable potion does not

in_game_claim: Greatly helps health and stamina (drunk in potions)
real_world_finding: The root contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids that are liver-toxic when taken by mouth; EMA allows external use only
rule_direction: Possible class B rule: repeated oral comfrey is harmful (direction only)

in_game_claim: Drives the urine strongly and purges the body
real_world_finding: EMA: traditional diuretic (flushing of the urinary tract) and mild digestive use
rule_direction: Diuretic effect is defensible

in_game_claim: Syrup drives away colds in long winters
real_world_finding: No evidence gathered for colds

in_game_claim: Miraculous for all eye ailments; compress relieves inflammation; sharper sight
real_world_finding: Used for conjunctivitis for decades; one prospective cohort trial reported recovery in most of 65 patients; a randomised trial in preterm neonates found no significant benefit on the main outcome; in-vitro anti-inflammatory signals; no evidence for sharper sight
rule_direction: Do not model a vision buff on evidence; anti-irritation use only

in_game_claim: Purifies blood; dispels dropsy and kidney stones
real_world_finding: Accepted use is mild to moderate depression (well-established use); the other claims are not accepted uses

in_game_claim: Brewed in wine it arms against all alcohol; in oil it prevents decay of meat
real_world_finding: No evidence gathered. Real risk: induces CYP3A4 and other enzymes, so it weakens many medicines; photosensitivity

in_game_claim: Placed on a wound it speeds recovery; ointment and bathing for skin
real_world_finding: EMA: minor skin inflammation, minor wounds, mouth and throat inflammation (topical)
rule_direction: Defensible for a healing or wound item; oral use is not the evidence base

in_game_claim: Good against cramps and for a medicinal drink
real_world_finding: Oral use for cramps is not an accepted EMA use

in_game_claim: Mulled with wine in the morning it prevents intoxication that day
real_world_finding: EMA accepts dyspepsia and flatulence (tea) for peppermint leaf; reviews find no effective hangover or intoxication remedy
rule_direction: Do not make mint reduce alcohol effects

in_game_claim: Poisonous; induces nausea and sleep; rarely deadly; used by old wives against headache
real_world_finding: Steroidal saponins; nausea, vomiting and other symptoms in large doses; berries and roots most toxic; deaths reported in children (secondary sources only)
rule_direction: Health loss and nausea are defensible; magnitude is a balance choice

in_game_claim: Brewed for little ones and the sick; puts anyone to sleep in dreamless darkness
real_world_finding: Opiate alkaloids; poppy preparations killed many infants historically; a series of poppy-intoxicated children had a high death rate
verdict: supported and more dangerous than the game says
rule_direction: Strong sedation is defensible; overdose risk is a real-world fact

in_game_claim: Less headache after alcohol; drinking too much dulls the mind; prophetic dreams
real_world_finding: EMA accepts mild dyspepsia and excessive sweating; thujone is neurotoxic (daily limit); hangover reviews found no effective herbal remedy

in_game_claim: Medicine against plague; relief from pain and poisoning in water; restores appetite in ale
real_world_finding: EMA accepts temporary loss of appetite and mild dyspepsia (traditional use)
verdict: appetite supported; plague and poisoning not supported
rule_direction: Appetite effect is defensible

in_game_claim: Pounded leaves on a wound stop bleeding at once
real_world_finding: Animal and lab studies suggest a haemostatic and wound-healing effect; no clinical evidence; a systematic review found no useful antibacterial leads
rule_direction: Mild styptic effect is a stretch; keep small

in_game_claim: Classified as poisonous in the game data
real_world_finding: EMA lists nettle leaf as a traditional herbal tea (urinary flushing, minor joint pain), which is hard to reconcile with a poisonous classification (our inference); the sting is a contact irritant
verdict: game flag differs from real life
rule_direction: Do not treat the poisonous flag as pharmacology

in_game_claim: Panacea; renews health; additive that arouses desire
real_world_finding: EMA: mild nervous tension and sleep problems, slow onset (2-4 weeks); NCCIH: value for insomnia not demonstrated; rare liver injury reported
rule_direction: Mild calming only; no healing claim

in_game_claim: Neutralises poisons (antidote recipes)
real_world_finding: Adsorbs many ingested toxins; volunteer studies show 74 % less absorption at 5 min, 47 % at 30 min, 40 % at 60 min, 16.5 % at 120 min; toxic alcohols and metals bind poorly and ethanol is not significantly blocked; routine use not recommended
rule_direction: Antidote effect is defensible; a time window would be realistic

in_game_claim: Ingredient of Dandelion syrup
real_world_finding: Cochrane: heals partial-thickness burns about 4-5 days faster than usual dressings (high quality); better than antiseptic washes for infected post-operative wounds (moderate quality); minor wounds unclear; venous leg ulcers no clear benefit and more pain (low quality)
rule_direction: Topical healing only; oral value is nutritional

in_game_claim: Ingredient of Bane potion and respec potion
real_world_finding: A. muscaria contains ibotenic acid and muscimol: drowsiness, delirium, nausea, sometimes seizures; usually resolves in about 24 h, rarely fatal. The in-game species is not stated
rule_direction: Sedation and confusion fit; lethal dose is not realistic for A. muscaria

in_game_claim: Alcohol 30-90 on the game scale
real_world_finding: Beer about 2-8 % ABV, wine 8-14 %, spirits 40-50 %; slivovitz 40-70 %. The game scale is relative, not percent
rule_direction: Keep the game 0-100 scale; use ABV only to rank drinks

in_game_claim: Param AlcoholDigestSpeedModfifOnFullStomache exists in the engine
real_world_finding: Food slows gastric emptying and delays alcohol absorption; peak blood alcohol is lower
rule_direction: Do not add a second food-alcohol rule; the engine has one

ingredient: Boar tooth / antlers / cobweb / cave mushroom
in_game_claim: Used as potion ingredients
real_world_finding: No real-world pharmacology gathered; treat as game fiction
